applicable_conditions: When attacking a defended surface group with limited point-defense magazines (as blue showed magazine depletion via chaff/SM-6 expenditure).
When the target is a high-value unit such as a carrier or destroyer with damage points above 1000.
When surface combatants have sufficient magazine capacity to fire 30+ missiles without exhausting their offensive loadout.
counter_conditions: If the blue force has unlimited point-defense ammunition or an AEGIS-like system with high engagement rates, saturation may still fail to achieve kill.
If enemy fighters intercept the surface missile salvos before terminal phase, as they did for J-15s.
If the targeted unit has a damage pool exceeding the maximum attainable missile damage, as seen with blue_cvn70 at 89% damage but not destroyed.
hypothesis: Increasing the fire quantity of surface-launched YJ-18 missiles to approximately 30 per attacking ship can significantly degrade or destroy defended naval targets, even when the carrier has strong point defenses, provided the weapons are concentrated on a single high-value unit.

steps: Assign each surface combatant a fire_quantity of 30 YJ-18, ensuring total missile loadout is sufficient.
Set attack delays to 5-10 seconds so all salvos arrive in a tight window.
Monitor enemy point-defense expenditure and be ready to follow up with a second wave.
recommended_pattern.summary: Use 27-30 YJ-18 missiles from each of three surface ships, all targeted on a single high-value unit, with salvos launched nearly simultaneously to overwhelm point defenses.
